title: Behold, Where, in a Mortal Form
description: Behold, Where, in a Mortal Form in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Enfield wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 239 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold, where, in a mor-tal form, Ap-pears each grace di-vine; The vir-tues, all in Je-sus met, With mil-dest ra-diance shine.

lines: Behold, where, in a mortal form,
The virtues, all in Jesus met,
To spread the rays of heavenly light,
To preach glad tidings to the poor,
His foes, ungrateful, sought his life;
In the last hour of deep distress,
With soul resigned, he bowed, and said,
Be Christ our pattern and our guide!
O, may we tread his holy steps,

licence: Public domain: William Enfield died in 1797.
credits: Words by William Enfield (1741–1797), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
